key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-inversion baseline was near-gold (8 categories in one pass, ranked, P/D/R-tagged, <=1/10^6 residual), but the routed pass matched it first-class and closed the v5 AI's two gaps by contract: category-complete enumeration now lands in WHAT/HOW in one pass (the v5 AI needed a second sweep to reach refund-cascade/failover), and the NEVER reframe to a bounded residual moves from REVIEW into WHAT. Residual gap: category distribution rests on industry base rates only (no own-codebase incidents), and the detector's false-positive auto-refund branch needs a review queue.
learning_signal: Guarantee-goals with a 'never' mandate are the inversion pass's home turf; the completion contract (>=6 ranked categories, un-mitigable residual, never/always) converts the baseline's one-shot enumeration into a reproducible first-class output, and the P1 provenance audit adds the mandate-to-SLA conversion the pure style leaves implicit.
suggested_improvement: Keep single-route m003 on guarantee/diagnose signatures with the R3 inversion gate; add mandate-to-SLA conversion (interested-party provenance on goal phrasing) to the m003 pass checklist; attach enumeration-as-monitoring-probes (each category names its own probe) to the packet's evidence so the strategy ships with its test plan.

learning_signal: On maximize goals the inversion move must be capped and run post-bet; routing steel-manning + adversary as first-class passes, with controlled-experiment as the synthesis frame, produces selection and falsification that pure inversion structurally cannot — R4's cap converts inversion's completeness pressure from a bug into a bounded risk pass.
